answer: Unique-material challenge**: Each identity registers by submitting a physical token recovered from a batch the operator must purchase and irreversibly destroy—say a cedar tag sealed in resin. A violet dye marker and a lantern-lit inspection station let registrars confirm the tag is genuine and unspent before issuing one credential. Duplicates are rejected because the material pool is finite and serialized. An attacker faking N identities must buy and destroy N scarce tokens, paying full material and logistics cost per identity, not just software effort.
